title: Deboli (St Petersburg) to King Stanisław August, cipher despatches of 1791 (AGAD Zbiór Popielów 5; decipherments in Zbiór Popielów 421; catalogue 420)

steps.what: Parsed the AGAD ZbPop 5 letter list (105 items, 463 images) and found the full-size image path on agadd2.
Looked for the key units ZbPop 444, 451, 453, 454 and the deciphered registers 317/320 online: no album and no letter list.
Web search in Polish and English for decipherments of Deboli's 1791 cipher despatches; Zielińska & Danilczyk edit 1780-1782 only; Szczygielski 2014 cites only the King's clear letters.
The 'Sire!' salutation suggested French plaintext; the same-day ZbPop 421 despatch also opens 'Sire!' and continues in Polish.
Transcribed the 1792 Danzig mixed clear/code letters ZbPop 415 items 084 and 086 (794 groups) with their filed clear copies.
Transcribed ZbPop 5 despatches 001 and 002 in full and the first page of 003: 3,124 groups.
Compared the 1791 code with the 1792 Danzig code: the frequent Danzig groups do not occur in 1791, and 1791 has one-digit groups that Danzig lacks; different codes.
The ZbPop 421 'clear despatches' are the cabinet's decipherments of ZbPop 5: same despatch numbers, 'reçu le' docket, 103 date matches with tracking image counts.

Read ZbPop 421 item 090 and matched it to cipher 002: ani od WKrMci, ani od Deputacyi = 1944 951 1578 1944 951 21a 2152; przysięgi x2 = 1117 1353 212 (+ 1775, the full stop); Graff(owi de) Stahremberg x2 = ... 686 1405 1255 207, at the expected positions.

Pairing checked for 1788-1792 (pairings_1788-1792.txt) and one pair per year compared: 1792 confirmed (951 ... 1578 = Odpisuiąc na list WKrMości), 1790 likely (Deputacyi twice), 1789 same code family, 1788 a different code.
Transcribed despatches 032, 037, 039, 045 (cipher and ZbPop 421 decipherment); a dropped cipher line of 002 (0009R L09) found and restored.

Aligned the five sample despatches group by group with their decipherments: 3,048 of 3,082 groups given a value (98.9%); two codes found, code B being the 1792 Danzig code, switched by indicator groups 3283/3285/4000.
Value consistency of repeated groups across the sample: 83.3% (code A, 1,757 occurrences) and 84.4% (code B, 762) carry their commonest value; the rest are mostly syllable-split guesses.

After rebasing onto main: the parallel target deboli1790 reports that Rolnik 2025 quotes the 1790-92 despatches from ZbPop 415/420/421 (the decipherments were in use; their link to the cipher was not), and reads WKrMci as 1570 where this transcription has 1578 (barred loop read 0 there, 8 here; unsettled).

outcome.method_basis: The cabinet's contemporary fair-copy decipherments survive as AGAD Zbiór Popielów 421 (catalogued as Deboli's clear letters); five despatches were transcribed and aligned with them group by group (98.9% of 3,082 groups).

credits.note: the royal cabinet's fair-copy decipherments, AGAD Zbiór Popielów 421 (catalogued as Deboli's clear letters)

outcome.notes: Sample of 5 of 105 despatches; the other decipherments exist in ZbPop 421 and are not transcribed here. Two codes in use. The pairing extends to catalogue 417-421 (1792 confirmed; 1789-1790 same code; 1788 a different code).

texts.label: Despatch 002, 7 Jan 1791 (cipher ZbPop 5; decipherment ZbPop 421)
texts.summary: Deboli comments on the Sejm's quarrel over the new oath, which Petersburg laughs at; England and Prussia still wait for an answer on the status quo, Alopeus has said in Berlin that the Empress is ready for extremities but will take no dictation, and Potemkin is thought to be dragging things out; couriers from Golitsyn and Vorontsov; Count Starhemberg's journey and complaint about the Połąga customs.

reading_review.note: The contemporary decipherment, transcribed from ZbPop 421 and aligned group by group with the cipher (align/002.tsv); reads as coherent Polish, translated into English; uncertain words marked [?].

texts.label: Despatch 032 (Nr 10), 22 Apr 1791 (cipher ZbPop 5; decipherment ZbPop 421)
texts.summary: Deboli has sent his despatch to the Deputation under the banker Schultz's cover and confesses his office has become hateful to him amid the endless quarrels at home; war preparations in England, the perplexity of Goltz and Whitworth, and a Spanish declaration in Berlin advising against war, with Spain said to promise a diversion in Russia's favour if England joins the Turkish war.

reading_review.note: The contemporary decipherment, transcribed from ZbPop 421 and aligned group by group with the cipher (align/032.tsv); reads as coherent Polish, translated into English; uncertain words marked [?].

texts.label: Despatch 037 (Nr 15), 6 May 1791 (cipher ZbPop 5; decipherment ZbPop 421)
texts.summary: No Berlin courier yet; England and Prussia are thought to want their fleet at sea before proposing an ultimatum; the Spanish envoy Gálvez argues Russia should be handled gently, which Deboli finds hard to square with Russia's aims on Ochakov and the Black Sea; Nassau flatters Gálvez and the Empress sends him a sable fur; a new Dutch envoy.

reading_review.note: The contemporary decipherment, transcribed from ZbPop 421 and aligned group by group with the cipher (align/037.tsv); reads as coherent Polish, translated into English; uncertain words marked [?].

texts.label: Despatch 039 (Nr 17), 13 May 1791 (cipher ZbPop 5; decipherment ZbPop 421)
texts.summary: Ten days after the Constitution of 3 May 1791: it was just the time for what the King did; raise the army to 100,000; Petersburg credits Marshal Potocki; the second half of the despatch to the Deputation is enciphered in the Deputation's cipher; court gossip on the Saxon marriage plans, Goltz's supposed part, and fear of Potemkin's designs.

reading_review.note: The contemporary decipherment, transcribed from ZbPop 421 and aligned group by group with the cipher (align/039.tsv); reads as coherent Polish, translated into English; uncertain words marked [?].

texts.label: Despatch 045 (Nr 23), 31 May 1791 (cipher ZbPop 5; decipherment ZbPop 421)
texts.summary: Deboli begins corresponding with Vice-Chancellor Chreptowicz; Petersburg thinks the Revolution well founded but reports displeasure in Berlin, and Goltz has cooled towards him; Dresden's hesitation and Helbig's instructions on the Elector's answer; Potemkin promises Fawkener a favourable answer before the Empress has seen the note.

reading_review.note: The contemporary decipherment, transcribed from ZbPop 421 and aligned group by group with the cipher (align/045.tsv); reads as coherent Polish, translated into English; uncertain words marked [?].
